title: Save, run, read output

outcomes.can: Predict the lines a short program prints, in order.
Find the line a compiler error names and repair it.
Print an exact two-line message from a written description.

intro: Every exercise in this course works the same way: you edit a file, save it, and read what comes back. This module covers that loop: printing a line, reading the output, and reading a compiler error.

steps.title: Save a file and read its output
steps.text: A C# program is a list of statements that run from top to bottom. Console.WriteLine("Ready"); is one statement. It prints the text between the double quotes, then ends the line. The semicolon ends the statement. When you save an exercise, the checker compiles your code, runs it, and compares the result with what the task asked for. Compiling means the C# compiler reads the whole file first. If it finds an error, nothing runs.

steps.title: Predict before running
steps.text: Read the example and predict its output before you run it.

steps.title: Trace the example
steps.text: The two statements ran in the order they were written, and each printed on its own line. The quotes mark where the text starts and stops. They are not printed. Output must match exactly: capital letters, spaces and punctuation all count.

steps.title: Predict a compiler error
steps.text: One statement in this example is not finished. Read it before checking.

steps.title: Read the compiler error
steps.text: Check the example. The compiler reports CS1002: ; expected. The numbers in brackets after the file name are the line and the column where it noticed the problem. Line 1 has no semicolon, so nothing ran, not even line 2. Every compiler error has a code such as CS1002 and names a line. Start reading at that line.

steps.title: Repair the first message
steps.text: Save the starter as it is and read the error. Fix that line, save again, and compare the output with the prompt.

steps.title: Print the board sign
steps.text: Work from the prompt. Save to check your output.

choices.text: Ready, then Open, on two lines
choices.feedback: Each Console.WriteLine prints its text and ends the line.
Console.WriteLine ends the line after its text, so the next print starts a new line.
Statements run from top to bottom, in the order they are written.

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.text: It prints Ready, then reports an error.
choices.feedback: The compiler reads the whole file before running anything. With an error, nothing runs.

choices.text: The compiler reports an error on line 1 and nothing prints.
choices.feedback: Line 1 is missing its semicolon. That is CS1002, and the program never starts.

choices.text: It prints Ready and Open, because line 2 is complete.
choices.feedback: One unfinished statement stops the whole file from compiling.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.
